content: Lansoprazole is a medication prescribed to treat several conditions. It is used to manage ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and conditions where the stomach produces excessive acid, such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. GERD occurs when stomach acid flows backward into the esophagus, causing heartburn and potential damage to the esophageal lining. Lansoprazole is also used in combination with other medications to eradicate Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori), a bacterium that contributes to the development of ulcers. This medication belongs to a class of drugs known as proton-pump inhibitors (PPIs), which work by reducing the production of stomach acid. Lansoprazole is available in two forms: delayed-release capsules and granules that can be mixed to create a delayed-release liquid solution. It is typically taken once daily before meals. However, when used in combination therapy to treat H. pylori, it may be taken twice daily (every 12 hours) or three times daily (every 8 hours) for a duration of 10 to 14 days. Always follow the instructions provided on your prescription label and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not take more or less of the medication or use it more frequently than prescribed. The capsules should be swallowed whole. This mixture should be swallowed immediately without chewing or crushing the granules. Alternatively, the granules can be mixed with 2 ounces of orange juice or tomato juice, stirred briefly, and consumed immediately. The glass should then be rinsed with additional juice, which should also be consumed immediately. For patients with a nasogastric tube, the granules can be mixed with 40 mL of apple juice and administered through the tube, followed by flushing the tube with more apple juice. If using the oral solution, the contents of a packet should be emptied into a container with 2 tablespoons of water, stirred well, and consumed immediately. If granules remain, add more water, stir, and drink immediately. Do not use any liquids or foods other than water, and do not crush or chew the granules. Continue taking lansoprazole even if you feel better, and do not stop the medication without consulting your doctor. Lansoprazole may also be prescribed for other conditions. If you have questions about its use for other purposes, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Before starting lansoprazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to it or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Certain medications, such as ampicillin, digoxin, ketoconazole, theophylline, and iron-containing vitamins, may interact with lansoprazole, requiring dose adjustments or careful monitoring. If you are taking sucralfate, take it at least 30 minutes after lansoprazole. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have a history of liver or kidney disease, or if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking lansoprazole, notify your doctor immediately. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while taking lansoprazole. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Lansoprazole may cause side effects. Common side effects include stomach pain and diarrhea. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Additionally, if you experience any unusual or concerning symptoms while taking this medication, contact your doctor promptly. Store lansoprazole in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all scheduled appointments with your doctor while taking lansoprazole. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Lansoprazole is sold under several brand names, including Prevacid®, Prevacid® NapraPAC®, Prevacid® SoluTab®, and Prevpac®.
